note: This node asserts only the defining property of the minimum of a finite family of reals: for the finite nonempty index set {1, ..., m}, min_{1 <= j <= m} n_j exists and is a lower bound for every member of the family, hence min_{1 <= j <= m} n_j <= n_i for each i. This is immediate from the definition of minimum (a member of the set that is <= all members), and existence is guaranteed because a finite nonempty subset of a totally ordered set has a least element. No auxiliary hypotheses are needed — in particular the p_i play no role here — so the absence of cited dependencies is appropriate rather than a gap. The only implicit assumption is m >= 1, which is already carried by the ambient statement's indexing 1, ..., m and by the well-formedness of the expression min_{1 <= j <= m} n_j appearing in the node itself.
